requirements.note: All seven sections are present in an inset grouped list. Account has inline Name/Email text fields and Sign Out with an alert confirmation, which leads to a signed-out state with Sign In. Reading has a slider with A/A glyphs, a Font row, a segmented control and a preview card. Appearance has a Theme row, Library has Sort plus two switches, and the Notifications master switch reveals the time, three toggles and a footer. Storage shows Used, Books and Cache, and Clear Cache confirms with an alert, then shows 0 MB and disables the button. About has Version, Privacy and Terms pages and Rate the App.
Font, Theme and Sort push onto checkmark lists with a back button, the way iPhone Settings does. The reminder time uses the compact system DatePicker with wheels in a popover.
The preview changes typeface, size and line spacing live. A footer reads e.g. 'Georgia, 29 pt, relaxed spacing.'
After relaunch the name, font size, font, spacing, theme, sort, cellular, notifications, reminder time, sub-toggles and cleared cache were all kept.
Reset is at the bottom with a Cancel/Reset alert. It restored every setting and kept the account, as its footer says.

bugs: Rate the App shows a home-made 'Enjoying Paperback?' alert. 'Rate Now' only adds a 'Thanks for rating' footer; no system review prompt or store page appears.
tells: Rating uses a custom pre-prompt alert instead of the system StoreKit review sheet.
Turning notifications on never asks for iOS notification permission.
The Sepia theme only tints the preview card; the rest of the screen stays plain light.
The Privacy and Terms pages repeat the nav-bar title as a large bold heading in the body.
In the signed-out Account card the explanation text sits almost against the top edge of the card, with too little padding.
At the largest text size the inline Name and Email fields cut their values off with an ellipsis ('Jordan Read…', 'jordan@pape…').
A.scroll: The scroll is a native collection view: smooth drags, flings with normal deceleration, rubber-band past the top, a blurred scroll-edge nav bar, and position kept after pushing and popping pickers. No blank rows or rows popping in.

requirements.note: All sections are present. Account has an avatar row (initials) that pushes an editable Account page, and Sign Out confirms with a system confirmation dialog. The signed-out state offers Sign In, which opens a real sheet with Name, Email, Password, Cancel and a disabled-until-valid Sign In. Reading has a slider, a Font row, a segmented control and a 'Chapter 1' preview. Appearance is an inline checkmark list with swatches. The Notifications master switch reveals the time, three toggles and a footer that tracks the time. Storage has a Books/Cache usage bar, and Clear Cache confirms in a dialog that names the size, then shows Zero KB and disables the button. About has Version, Privacy and Terms pages and Rate Paperback.
Font and Sort push onto checkmark lists that pop back automatically after a choice. Theme is an inline checkmark list. The time uses the compact system DatePicker.
The preview reflects font, size and spacing live, and its accessibility value describes the current settings.
After relaunch the edited name, size 29, Georgia, Relaxed, Sepia, Author sort, cellular, notifications at 10:00 PM, cleared cache and signed-out state were all kept.
Reset All Settings is a centred destructive button with a confirmation dialog. It restored all defaults, kept the account, and the footer changes to 'All settings are at their defaults.'

tells: The coloured dot in the storage legend does not grow with Dynamic Type; at the largest size it is tiny beside the text.
In dark mode the preview cell is a slightly different shade from the rest of the Reading card, which leaves a visible seam.
At the largest text size the email under the account name is middle-truncated ('alex.morg…ample.com').
B.scroll: The scroll is a native collection view: smooth drags and flings, rubber-band at both ends, a blurred scroll-edge nav bar, and position kept across push/pop. No blank or popping rows.

why: Both apps meet every requirement with native lists, pickers, switches and persistence, and neither has a functional bug in the spec items. B goes further in system ways: real notification-permission and StoreKit review prompts, a Sepia theme that tints the whole screen, a proper sign-in sheet and account page, and a storage usage bar. A instead uses a custom rating pre-prompt, never asks for notification permission, and its Sepia only tints the preview.
